L4.01.title: Cars in the Yard (ar extended)
L4.01.goal: Review **ar** (/ar/ as in *car*, taught in Level 3.08) and extend it to
L4.01.newToday: nothing brand-new at the grapheme level — this lesson's job is fluency and range: single-syllable ar review → confident multisyllabic ar words, both closed-first- syllable (gar-den) and ar-first-syllable (tar-get) shapes.
L4.01.heartLine: none new — review *are, water, once, only*

read.A: Sam and his dad live on a farm. At dark, they walk to the yard. Sam can see a big, bright star. "That star is so very far," Dad said. Sam runs to get his cart. He puts a jar, a hard hat, and a sharp pencil in the cart. He wants to make a star chart. Dad helps Sam mark each star on the chart. "You are a smart artist," Dad said. Sam grins. The farm is still, and the stars spark and shine in the dark yard.
read.B: Mr. Khan drives his car to the market. He must park in the car park at the back. It is hard to find a spot — the car park is full. At last, Mr. Khan spots a gap by the yard. He parks his car, locks it, and walks to the market. He needs a jar of jam, a sharp pencil, and a tiny chart for his garden. On the way back, a spark of light catches his eye — the sun is starting to sink behind the dark market roofs. Mr. Khan is glad he did not start so late.

L4.02.title: The Fork in the Road (or/ore extended + the war/wor quirk)
L4.02.goal: Review **or** and **ore** (/or/ as in *for* and *more*, taught in Level 3.09), extend to multisyllabic or/ore words, and meet today's genuinely new content: the **war/wor quirk** — when w sits right before or, the vowel sound shifts (*war* → /wor/, *work* → /wer/), even though the spelling still uses the familiar "or."
L4.02.newToday: the war/wor quirk (warm, war, work, word, world)

read.A: It is harvest time on the farm. Dad and Sam load the cart before the storm starts. Sam picks corn from the yard. His dog Storm (yes, that is her name!) runs to the barn. "A storm is coming, Storm!" Sam yells. The wind is strong, and rain starts to come down fast. Dad and Sam sort the corn and put it in the fort — a tiny shed by the barn. Storm the dog barks at the wind. Soon the storm is gone, and the sun shows itself again from the north. "That was a short storm," Sam says. "More corn for us to sort tomorrow."
read.B: Amina drives north for work. Before she starts the car, she checks the horn and the fuel. The road has a fork — one way goes north, one goes to the port. Amina picks the north road. A storm starts, and rain comes down hard and hits the window. Amina slows the car and clicks on the lights. At last, she spots the store where she must stop for parts for the fort's old gate. She picks four parts, pays, and starts the drive back. "That was a short but hard trip," she tells her boss. "I will need more time for the next one."

L4.03.title: Her First Bird
L4.03.goal: Read and spell words with **er, ir, ur** — three spellings, one sound: /er/.

read.A: It was winter. Nadia's dad set up a bird perch by the porch. Nadia sat still, waiting for her first bird to land. First a big black bird sat on the fence. Then a tiny bird with a red chest came to perch. "Look! Its chirp is so soft," Nadia said. Her sister ran to see too. "Don't stir, or it will fly off," Nadia told her. The bird did not fly off — it stayed and had a drink, then flew off with a quick turn. Nadia and her sister sat under the tree until the sun went down.
read.B: Bilal is a nurse. His shift starts at sunup. First, he checks each person's chart. Then he helps a girl with a hurt arm — she fell by the curb and needs a splint. "Try not to stir it too much," Bilal tells her. Her mother sits with her, holding her purse. Later, an older man comes in with a bad thirst and a fever. Bilal checks his term of illness and rings the doctor. By the end of his shift, Bilal is tired, but glad he could help. "Nursing is hard work," he tells his sister that night, "but I would not turn back."

L4.04.title: Fair Weather, Rare Deer
L4.04.goal: Read and spell words with **air, are, ear, eer** (all /air/ or /eer/ sounds); review the **war/wor** quirk (taught in 4.2) alongside them, since all of today's material is other vowel-r teams.

read.A: On a cold, clear day, Hina and her dad hike near the hills. Hina wears a warm coat and a hat, but no gloves — she likes to feel the crisp air. "Look — a deer!" Dad says, showing her. It is a rare deer with pale hair on its back. The deer does not run. It stares at Hina, its ears turning this way and that. Hina stands still and does not dare move. After a year of hiking with her dad, this is the closest she has come to a deer. "I will never forget this," Hina says. On the walk back, they share a pear and talk of the deer the whole way home.
read.B: Farah works at a tiny shop that sells chairs and tables. It is a warm day, and the work is hard. A pair of chairs must be moved to the back room, and Farah has to clear a path first. "Be careful — that chair leg is not square," her boss warns. Farah takes care, but her arms still hurt by the end of her shift. By closing time, a man comes in to buy a rare, old chair worth a fair price. Farah helps him carry it to his car. "That was the worst part of my day, but also the best sale," she tells her sister that night, and they share a laugh.

L4.05.title: The Noisy Boy
L4.05.goal: Read and spell words with the diphthong **oi** and **oy** (one sound, two spellings).
L4.05.heartLine: none new — review *once, boy(not a heart word — decodable now, see note)*

read.A: Zayn is a boy who makes a lot of noise. In class, his choice seat is next to the window, and he likes to spot every bird, truck, and train he sees. "Zayn, use a soft voice," his teacher says. At recess, Zayn and his friends toss a coin to pick a game. "Heads, we play tag. Tails, we play with the toy trucks," Zayn says. The coin lands on tails. Zayn grins big and runs to get the toy box. His friend Roy joins in, and soon the whole class is enjoying the game. By the end of recess, Zayn's voice is quite tired from cheering.
read.B: Tariq works at a shop that fixes engines. Today, he must make a choice: fix an old engine's oil leak, or help a customer who needs a new coin battery for her car key. His boss, Mr. Roy, tells him to help the customer first. Tariq checks the car key, finds the right coin battery, and fits it in. "That should not annoy you again," he tells her. Then Tariq turns to the oil leak — it takes him a good while to find the moist patch under the engine and seal the joint. By the end of the day, Tariq feels the joy of a job done well, even when his voice is tired from talking to so many customers.

L4.06.title: Loud Clouds, Slow Cows
L4.06.goal: Read and spell words with the diphthong **ou** and **ow** (/ow/ as in *out* and *cow* — a different sound from the /ō/ ow the learner already knows from *snow*).

read.A: It was a bright, loud day at the county fair. Bilal and his mom walked past a brown cow, a tiny mouse in a cage, and a fluffy owl blinking in the sun. Then a clown in a big gown and a bright crown came by, honking a horn. "That is so loud!" Bilal said, covering his mouth. The clown made a crowd of kids laugh out loud. A dog started to howl at the clown's honking horn, and an owl in a nearby cage let out a soft growl-like hoot. Bilal counted five clowns before he and his mom found their way to the food stand for a snack.
read.B: It is a hot day, and Naveed is at work downtown when the power goes out. The whole office is dark, and a loud, low sound comes from the backup generator switching on. "How long will this last?" a coworker asks. Naveed checks his device — no signal, either. He walks down to the ground floor, where a tiny crowd has formed near the front doors. Someone found a radio and is counting down the minutes until the power comes back. After about an hour, the lights come back on, and a round of quiet cheers moves across the crowd. "I am proud we stayed so calm," Naveed's boss says as everyone heads back to their desks.

L4.07.title: Paw, Pause, and the Mall
L4.07.goal: Read and spell words with **aw, au, al(l)** — all spelling the same /aw/ sound.

read.A: At dawn, Zara and her granddad walk to the small lawn behind their house. A hawk lands on the old wall, its claw gripping the stone. "Don't move, or you'll cause it to fly off," her granddad whispers. Zara stands tall and still. The hawk turns its head, gives a small yawn, and looks right at her. Then it spreads its wings and flies over the mall down the road. "That was worth the early start!" Zara says. On the walk back, they talk about hawks and how they hunt. Zara makes a quick drawing of the hawk in her notebook before her meal.
read.B: Mariam works at a small shop inside the mall. Business is slow, so she and her coworker take a pause to talk. "I saw a hawk on my walk to work this morning," Mariam says. "That's rare for downtown," her coworker replies. At noon, a small fault in the mall's power system causes all the lights to flicker, and a loud alarm sounds. "Don't fall over anyone — stay calm and walk to the hall," a staff member calls out. After a short pause, the power comes back, and the alarm stops. "Well, that was not part of the plan," Mariam laughs, and they get back to work.

L4.08.title: Bread and Silent Letters
L4.08.goal: Read and spell words with **ea saying /ĕ/** (as in *bread*), and four silent-letter patterns: **kn, wr, gn, mb**.

read.A: "Get ready — the weather is turning," Dad said, looking at the heavy gray clouds. Sana ran to get her coat. She had a small cut on her knee from playing outside, so Dad helped clean it first. "Don't rub it with dirty hands," he said, wrapping a bandage around her knee. Sana took a deep breath and looked out the window. Wind began to shake the thread-thin branches of the old tree. "I meant to bring in the washing before this," Mom said, dashing outside. By the time she got back, her hair was a mess, but the washing was safe and dry. That night, the family sat close, listening to the storm, glad to be warm and healthy inside.
read.B: Rashid was driving to a job site when he took a wrong turn onto a bumpy road. His truck hit a deep rut, and his wrist twisted hard against the wheel. "That's not good," he said, feeling a sharp pain. He pulled over, took a breath, and checked his wrist — it was already starting to swell. Rashid called his boss to explain he would be late. At the clinic, a nurse wrapped his wrist and told him to rest it. "You're lucky it's not broken," she said. Rashid signed the form, thanked her, and called his boss again with an update. It was a hard start to the day, but he stayed calm and got past it.

L4.09.title: Phones, Photos, and Ghosts
L4.09.goal: Read and spell words with **ph** (/f/), **ch** saying /k/ or /sh/ (not just its usual /ch/), and **gh** (as /g/ in *ghost*, and as /f/ in *rough, tough, enough, cough*).
L4.09.heartLine: none new — review *laugh* (already known — now explainable!)

read.A: At school, Miss Amna told a ghost story before lunch. "This school used to be a farmhouse," she said, "and some say a ghost still walks the halls at night." Hamza's stomach did a quick flip. "Is it true?" he asked. "Maybe," Miss Amna said with a grin, "or maybe it's just an old tale." At recess, Hamza and his friends took a photo of the old, dusty hallway, hoping to catch something strange in the photo. They didn't see a ghost, but they did find an old graph pinned to a wall, showing how many students went to the school long ago. It was a rough, faded page, but Hamza's teacher said it was a real piece of history. Hamza laughed, his stomach finally calm again.
read.B: Dr. Farid works at a small clinic. Today has been a tough day — the phone has not stopped ringing. A patient calls to ask if her cough is bad enough to come in. "It sounds rough," Dr. Farid says, "come in and I will check your chest with a stethoscope." Later, a machine in the clinic breaks down, and Dr. Farid must call for a repair. He takes a photo of the broken part to send to the repair shop. By the end of his shift, his stomach aches from stress, but he still has enough energy to smile at his last patient. "Tough day," he tells his wife that night, "but a good one."

L4.10.title: Little Candle, Little Table
L4.10.goal: Read and spell two-syllable words ending in **consonant + le** (the sixth and last syllable type: candle, table, little).

read.A: Maya's uncle made her a little purple table for her room. It was simple but sturdy, with four short legs and a smooth top. "You can put your candle, your puzzle, and your bottle of paint on it," her uncle said. Maya set a small candle in the middle, next to a puzzle piece shaped like an apple. Her little sister Zoe came in, saw the table, and let out a giggle. "Can I have a table too, Uncle?" Zoe asked. "Maybe a purple one for you as well," he said with a smile. That night, Maya sat at her little table and worked on her puzzle until she could hardly keep her eyes open.
read.B: At the repair shop, Bilal is asked to fix a wobbly table for a customer. One leg is a little shorter than the others, and the handle on the drawer has come loose. Bilal takes a sample of the wood to check the color match, then tightens the handle with a small tool. He turns the table upside down and adds a thin block under the short leg so it no longer wobbles. "It was a simple fix," Bilal tells the customer when she comes to collect it, "but I wanted to be sure it was sturdy before you took it home." The customer checks the table, gives it a gentle push, and smiles — no wobble at all.

L4.11.title: A Nation's Vision
L4.11.goal: Read words with five common Latin/French endings: **-tion, -sion, -ture, -ous, -cial/-tial** — the endings that show up constantly in longer, more grown-up words.

read.A: On a school trip to the nature center, Bina's class saw a strange creature in a tank. "Pay attention," her teacher said, "this fish is famous for its unusual motion — watch how it moves." Bina leaned in, curious, and took a picture with her class tablet. The creature was not dangerous, the guide explained, just shy. "It hides when there's too much attention on it," the guide said. Bina made a decision: she would ask her question quietly. "What does it eat?" she whispered. The guide smiled at her care and gave a full explanation. Bina felt she had learned something special about nature that day, and she couldn't wait to share her picture with her family.
read.B: Dr. Rehman starts a special session with a new patient today. "I want to give you my full attention," she says, "so let's talk about your question in detail." The patient explains a mixture of symptoms — some minor, some she's nervous about. Dr. Rehman takes note of each one with care, then explains her decision: a short series of tests, plus a change in diet. "This plan should not cause any confusion," Dr. Rehman says, "and I will check on you next session." The patient feels reassured by Dr. Rehman's calm, generous attention. "Thank you for taking this so seriously," she says as she leaves. Dr. Rehman notes the session in the patient's official file before her next appointment.

L4.12.title: Breaking Words Apart
L4.12.goal: Learn to divide two-syllable words into chunks using three patterns — **VC/CV**,
L4.12.newToday: syllable division (VC/CV, V/CV, VC/V — the "flex rule"), schwa

read.A: Layla found a small spider in her picnic basket. "Don't be scared," her mother said, "it's just a garden spider — it won't hurt you." Layla watched the spider a moment, then gently tipped the basket so it could climb onto a napkin and off into the garden. "That spider has seven legs left — maybe it lost one," Layla noticed. Her mother explained that spiders often have eight legs, but this one must have had an accident. At the picnic, Layla ate a muffin and told everyone about the seven-legged spider. "People at school won't believe this," she laughed, already planning how she'd tell the story tomorrow.
read.B: Rukhsana and her husband rent a small cabin by the river for the weekend. It is a simple place — one room, a basket for firewood, and a helmet hanging by the door for the rental kayak. On the first evening, they spot a robin building a nest near the window. "That's a good sign," Rukhsana's husband says. "A robin near your cabin means good luck, my mother used to say." They spend the visit reading, cooking simple meals, and watching the river. Before they leave, Rukhsana notices the robin has finished its nest. "I hope it's safe here," she says, already planning to visit again — maybe with enough money saved for a full week next time.

L4.13.title: Running, Happier, Hoping
L4.13.goal: Learn three spelling rules for adding suffixes: the **1-1-1 doubling rule**, the
L4.13.newToday: 1-1-1 doubling rule, change-y-to-i rule; drop-e reviewed

read.A: Iman's puppy, Buttons, was getting bigger every week. "He's the funniest, wobbliest puppy on the street," Iman's dad said, laughing as Buttons went running and slipping across the kitchen floor. Iman had been hoping for a puppy for months, and now she was caring for Buttons every day — feeding him, walking him, and studying every trick in her puppy training book. "He's not the smartest puppy," Iman admitted, "but he's trying." One evening, Buttons started chasing his tail, spinning and tripping until he flopped down, dizzy. Iman and her family were all crying with laughter. "That was the funniest thing I've seen all week," her mom said, still wiping tears from laughing so hard.
read.B: Sarah has been studying at night, hoping for a bigger role at her company. She has been carrying a heavy load — working her regular shift, then studying for two hours before bed. "It's the hardest I've ever tried at anything," she tells her sister, tapping her pencil, stopping only to stretch her tired hands. Her manager, impressed by how she's been performing, mentions she is planning to recommend Sarah for the new position. "You've been working harder than anyone else on the team," her manager says. Sarah feels her effort paying off — she keeps studying, knowing the extra work is worth it for a chance at something bigger.

L4.14.title: The Word-Attack Routine
L4.14.goal: Put every syllable-type, syllable-division, and morphology skill from Level 4 together into one repeatable routine for decoding ANY long, unfamiliar word — real or made-up.
L4.14.newToday: the five-step word-attack routine (mark → peel → chunk → blend → flex)

read.A: In her story, Amina wrote about a robot named Blip who was the unhappiest robot in the whole factory. Blip kept restarting himself, hoping a reboot would fix his mood, but nothing changed. One day, an engineer noticed Blip's wiring was disconnected in one small spot. After reconnecting it, Blip stopped feeling unfriendly toward the other robots and started reporting for his shift with a smile. "Sometimes the unhappiest robot just needs the right person to notice the disconnection," Amina's teacher said when she read the story aloud. Amina's classmates loved it, especially the part where Blip went from unfriendly to the friendliest robot in the whole story.
read.B: At the office, the internet has been nonstop unreliable all morning. Farah, the IT support worker, starts by reconsidering the whole network setup instead of just restarting each computer one by one. She finds that a cable was quietly disconnected behind a desk — someone had bumped it while unpacking a delivery. After reconnecting it, she spends an hour retesting every computer, reporting her findings to her manager as she goes. "This was more than a quick fix," she tells her manager, "it needed real troubleshooting, not just restarting things and hoping." Her manager thanks her for being so thorough, and by the afternoon, the whole office is back online, no longer disconnected.

L4.15.title: Reading the Real World
L4.15.goal: Read the first fully authentic, non-controlled texts in the course — a real notice, a recipe, and a short news paragraph — and learn the exact, no-guessing protocol for handling a genuinely unknown word in real text.
L4.15.newToday: the off-ramp — authentic text + the "stop, don't guess" unknown-word protocol
L4.15.heartLine: none new — this lesson uses whatever heart words naturally appear in authentic text, flagged as met, not pre-taught

L4.16.title: Level 4 Mastery Check
L4.16.goal: Confirm the learner has mastered every Level 4 pattern and the word-attack routine well enough to move to Level 5 (Word Power & Fluency), which shifts from controlled decodable text to wide reading.
L4.16.newToday: nothing new — this is a consolidation + testing lesson
